title: FirstPaycheck evaluation case
description: One question a new hire asks, the documents and profile it depends on, and the answer the user confirmed. eval/run.py grades the agent and the no-tools baseline against these. A case passes when every graded figure is within its tolerance and every must_include point is covered. See eval/README.md.

id.description: Matches the file name without .json, e.g. ex1-take-home.

example.description: Appendix A example number, for the five proposal examples and their variants.

variant_of.description: id of the case this one changes (an edge case or a different document set).

analysis.description: Which analysis the case scores. eval/run.py reports a pass rate per analysis. Matches the calculator names in the proposal.

question.description: Exactly what the new hire asks.

source.description: Where the question came from: 'proposal Appendix A', 'interview <date>', 'edge case'. No names of real people.

status.description: draft = hand-computed, not yet judged by a new hire. user_confirmed = a new hire judged this answer right.

confirmed_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD the user confirmed it. Required when status is user_confirmed.

tax_year.description: Tax tables and limits the figures use. Re-check every figure when this changes.

docs.description: Document file names the agent gets, e.g. benefits_guide.pdf. Files in samples/ unless the case notes say otherwise.

profile.description: Name of a file in eval/profiles/ without .json.

profile_overrides.description: Keys that replace the named profile's values for this case only (shallow merge).

fields.description: Extracted document fields the answer depends on. A string is a field id from samples/answers/*.json (resolved by the loader). An object is an inline field, using docs/fields.schema.json's shape, for documents with no answer file yet.

figures.description: Every number the answer should state, plus the inputs they come from (graded: false).

must_include.description: Points a correct answer covers. Each is judged present or missing.

must_not_include.description: Claims that make the answer wrong, e.g. 'always buy'.

citations.description: Pages the answer must link to. Also the retrieval check: each page is in the search tool's top 3.

tools.description: Calculator tools the agent should call (names from the proposal: paycheck, benefits_cost, contribution_order, espp, loan_vs_invest, offer_compare, search_documents).

asks_for.description: Inputs the agent must ask the user for instead of guessing (missing or unconfirmed). When set, figures may be empty.

assumptions.description: Choices made to get one right answer (W-4 settings, what a low-use year means). A teammate changing one must re-derive the figures.

sources.description: Official source for every rate or limit the figures use.

id.description: Name used in other figures' derivations.

label.description: How the answer should name it.

graded.description: false for inputs and intermediate steps the answer need not state.

tolerance.description: Allowed difference. Defaults to 1.00 for usd units (the proposal's $1 rule) and 0 otherwise.

derivation.description: Arithmetic over other figure ids and numbers (+ - * / parentheses, min, max). The test suite recomputes it, rounds to cents, and checks it equals value.

from_field.description: Field id this input comes from; value must equal that field's value.

from_profile.description: Profile key this input comes from; value must equal it.
